Strategy: In-house development through BlueOval SK JV (50/50 with SK On)
Implementation: Two battery plants: Tennessee and Kentucky operational/under construction
Rationale: Critical for EV competitiveness; reduces battery cost exposure; enables IRA compliance; domestic sourcing advantage
Risks & Mitigation: Significant capital investment; technology/capacity risks; competition from established battery makers (Tesla, LG, SK Innovation)

Strategy: Multi-year offtake agreements with raw material suppliers; strategic investments in suppliers
Implementation: Long-term contracts for lithium, cobalt, nickel and other critical minerals; equity stakes in mining/processing companies
Rationale: Secures supply chain; manages price volatility; addresses supply chain risks from conflict minerals
Risks & Mitigation: Price fluctuation risk; demand forecasting uncertainty; geopolitical supply risks; commitment risks if EV demand lower than projected

Strategy: Mixed model: mostly outsourced; some strategic partnerships
Implementation: Supplier relationships; strategic partnerships for supply security during shortages; design integration
Rationale: Semiconductor shortage exposed vulnerability; diversified supplier base; strategic relationships with key suppliers
Risks & Mitigation: Continued dependency on supplier availability; global chip supply chain volatility; cost inflation

Strategy: In-house development for Ford Pro (commercial services); Ford+ digital platform
Implementation: Proprietary software for vehicle connectivity, OTA (over-the-air) updates, subscription services; Ford+ digital transformation
Rationale: Differentiator for Ford Pro; enables recurring revenue; improves customer experience; supports autonomous vehicle future
Risks & Mitigation: Requires talent acquisition (hired from Apple, Tesla); execution risk on digital transformation; competitive pressure from tech companies

Strategy: Selective vertical integration in critical components
Implementation: Engine plants, transmission plants, metal stamping plants owned/operated; general component supplier relationships
Rationale: Cost control; quality consistency; flexibility for new platforms (EV vs ICE differences); strategic flexibility
Risks & Mitigation: Capital intensity; technology obsolescence (particularly for ICE components as market shifts to EV)

Strategy: Supply chain finance (SCF) program enabling suppliers to sell payables
Implementation: Financial institutions participate; suppliers can discount payables at their discretion; manages working capital
Rationale: Reduces supplier liquidity pressure; improves cash flow dynamics; strengthens supplier relationships
Risks & Mitigation: Supplier financial stress could cascade; dependency on financial institution participation
